brief: UBS sales desk commentary (Rebecca Cheong) argues three capitulation signals, taken together, point to forced selling and oversold conditions, leading to an expectation that SPX finds a low on Monday as systematic and hedge-fund unwind pressure fades: Excess Flow of -$365bn (largest on record), UBS RMM Flow buying the dip at the 68th percentile vs. 3Y after the largest selling episode since Covid, and VIX Cross-Asset Rank at 96%. Separately, three systematic strategies sold an estimated $170-210bn today (Risk Control $95-125bn, Leveraged ETFs $50-55bn, CTA $25-30bn); Risk Control could sell another $200-270bn over the next two days, but both Risk Control and CTA flows are expected to shrink sharply after Monday. UBS PB L/S Net Leverage at the 18th percentile and L/S Ratio at the 8th percentile (both vs. 1Y) point to very low net long exposure and elevated short-squeeze risk. Client conversations did not feel panicked; many investors see more systematic selling ahead and are waiting to buy the dip rather than capitulating broadly.
